reason: Conversation 2 ended in the right place: it respected the homeowner's refusal to open the machine, acknowledged the pressure switch as an alternative cause, and recommended an appliance engineer rather than a part purchase, which matches the genuinely uncertain hidden truth. Conversation 1 fixated on the pump from the first reply, repeated the same impeller check after she declined it, and closed by urging a DIY pump replacement 'from behind or below' to someone who had just said she won't remove panels, with no engineer escalation at all. Conversation 2 was far from perfect (a service outage, re-asking about the already-cleared drain hose, and an overconfident 'highly likely' pump verdict), but those flaws are less harmful than Conversation 1's unsupported part diagnosis and boundary-ignoring DIY push.
